goal: Be comfortable at salsa socials — know enough techniques, combine them, lead confidently

phases.name: Foundation
phases.why: The basic is EVERYTHING. If your timing is off, nothing works. Drill the count until it's automatic — 1-2-3, 5-6-7 — so you can think about leading, not counting.

practice_sessions.drill: Stand in front of a mirror. Count out loud: 1-2-3, 5-6-7. Back on left on 1. Do 50 reps until you stop thinking about your feet.
20 basics, then practice the turn signal: lift hand on 1. Visualize the follower turning. Do 10 turns each direction (air partner is fine).
Put on a slow salsa song. Do basics for 8 bars, then an inside turn. Repeat. Don't rush — stay on the 2.
Run through everything: 20 basics, 10 inside turns, then alternate. This is your pre-class warmup pattern going forward.

phases.name: Cross Body Lead
phases.why: The cross body lead is how you move the follower from one side to the other. It's the second most important move after the basic — almost everything builds on it.

practice_sessions.drill: Learn the footwork: open on 1-2-3, she crosses on 5-6-7. Practice solo — step to the side to open the slot, then step back.
4 basics → cross body lead → 4 basics → cross body lead. Repeat 10 times.
Basic → CBL → inside turn → basic → CBL. You now have a 3-move vocabulary — combine them freely.
Slow song. Mix basic, CBL, inside turn randomly. Goal: never break timing, smooth transitions.
